own_scenes.desc: En Estados Unidos la crítica, que detesta a Black Sabbath y a Judas Priest, evita el término «heavy metal» y prefiere «hard rock», el formato radiofónico de moda en los setenta, donde caben grupos muy populares que no cumplen del todo el código: Aerosmith (1973) y Kiss (1974) son demasiado melódicos para ser heavy en esa década. Cuando el género se fragmente, el lite metal adoptará su estilo vocal melódico y sus armonías, y ambos acabarán dentro del metal ampliado. Alice Cooper, que compartía cartel con Black Sabbath, regala al heavy la estética visual de película de terror.

notes.chapter: Cap. 4: Disfrutar la música: parias orgullosos
notes.text: Hasta un grupo marginal en el metal como Aerosmith tuvo en los setenta un público solo masculino: Tom Hamilton llamaba a sus fans «el ejército azul», estadios llenos de chicos en vaqueros.

refs.q: Groups such as Aerosmith (first release in 1973) and Kiss (first release in 1974) were too melodic to be considered heavy metal in the 1970s.
refs.para: The term “heavy metal” has been widely accepted in Britain but has met with some resistance in the United States. American critics, especially those who find groups such as Black Sabbath and Judas Priest to be repugnant—that is, who detest heavy metal—try not to use the term. Instead they employ a broader category, “hard rock,” in which heavy metal groups are included as a minor component with many others. In part, this usage is due to the wide popularity of the hard-rock radio format in the 1970s, when American critics were carefully attending to radio. Moreover, there were several very popular American bands that were similar to heavy metal groups but did not fully conform to heavy metal’s code. Groups such as Aerosmith (first release in 1973) and Kiss (first release in 1974) were too melodic to be considered heavy metal in the 1970s. The term “hard rock” accommodated them, along with purer heavy metal bands. When the genre of heavy metal fragmented in the mid-1980s, one segment, lite metal, embraced Aerosmith’s melodic vocal style while retaining specifically metal identifications, allowing Kiss and Aerosmith, which were still going strong in 1990, to be included in the now broadened metal genre. Still another reason for the American reluctance to employ “heavy metal” as a rubric is that the concert bills in the United States in the 1970s were not genre-specific. Heavy metal bands that toured the United States prior to 1979 did not use other, younger or less prominent heavy metal groups to open for them. There just were not many heavy metal bands in the United States at…
refs.chapter: Cap. 2: Heavy metal: la bestia que se niega a morir

refs.q: Alice Cooper, for example, can be credited with donating a horror-film visual aesthetic to heavy metal’s bag of tricks.
refs.para: The teaming of disparate types of bands on concert bills was responsible for the further development of the heavy metal genre. Bands had firsthand experience with musical styles that were close enough to their own to invite borrowing. Thus, new influences helped to shape heavy metal as the decade of the 1970s proceeded. Alice Cooper, for example, can be credited with donating a horror-film visual aesthetic to heavy metal’s bag of tricks. The dialogic process that creates a genre does not stop once that genre has crystallized. As George Lipsitz argues, “Popular music is nothing if not dialogic, the product of an ongoing historical conversation.”²⁷
refs.chapter: Cap. 2: Heavy metal: la bestia que se niega a morir

refs.q: “We used to call our fans the blue army, . . . We’d look out and all we’d see were these stadiums full of guys in bluejeans, a sea of blue.”
refs.para: “That the audience for heavy-metal music is heavily male-dominated is generally acknowledged, and statistically confirmed.”³⁰ Even a marginal metal group such as Aerosmith had an all-male following during the 1970s. Steve Tyler, the group’s singer, bluntly acknowledges this truth: “It used to be the only girls at Aerosmith shows were the ones who came to blow us on the bus.” His band mate, Tom Hamilton, agrees: “We used to call our fans the blue army, . . . We’d look out and all we’d see were these stadiums full of guys in bluejeans, a sea of blue.”³¹

similar_scenes.name: Hard rock
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: El hard rock marca el fin de los creativos sesenta: sigue basado en el blues, pero más rápido, ruidoso y fuerte, y entierra el sufrimiento negro bajo miles de decibelios. Precedido por Cream, Blue Cheer y Guess Who, lo definen Led Zeppelin, hijos del blues que lo tocan como música para el cuerpo y que imponen el LP como formato del rock. En Gran Bretaña, Free, Status Quo, Thin Lizzy, UFO, Uriah Heep, Slade, Faces, Deep Purple (el estereotipo del género), Black Sabbath (cimientos del black y el doom metal) y Queen, los bromistas del movimiento. En EE UU, Mountain, James Gang, Grand Funk Railroad, Montrose, Bachman-Turner Overdrive y Heart.

podcast.title: 1983 Musical Landscape
podcast.body: In 1983, one of the two dominant musical camps for musicians was "heavy, hard rock, charged up and testosterone," which stood in stark contrast to The Smiths' jangly pop sound. "If you were a musician in 1983, you were in one of two camps. A, you were into heavy, hard rock, charged up and testosterone..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: What's The Big Deal About The Smiths

podcast.title: Velvet Revolver Grammy Award (2004)
podcast.body: Velvet Revolver won a Grammy Award for Best Hard Rock Performance for their song "Fall To Pieces" from the album "Contraband." "I hit the contributor to VR winning a Grammy Award for Best Hard Rock Performance."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Scott Weiland: Part 3

podcast.title: "Satanist" Branding due to Association with Crime
podcast.body: Hard rock, along with metal, was a genre often viewed with suspicion and branded as "Satanist" by those who distrusted it, particularly after its association with serial killers like Richard Ramirez. The public reaction was fueled by the perception that the music could inspire evil. "for a time was branded as Satanists by people who distrusted hard rock and metal."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Murder Ballads (and Other Deadly Songs)

podcast.title: AC/DC Rule Origin
podcast.body: The hard rock band AC/DC lent its name to "The ACDC Rule," which states that the initial chart performance of a recording reflects the artist's last hit. This rule was coined because AC/DC's first and, for a long time, only number one album was the one released after their biggest seller, "Back in Black," illustrating how prior success influences subsequent chart entries. "I named it after ACDC because the hard rock bands first and for a long time only number one album was the LP after their biggest seller back in black."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Toppermost of the Poppermost Edition Part 1

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Toppermost of the Poppermost Edition Part 1

podcast.title: ACDC as Reference Standard
podcast.body: ACDC's "Back in Black" album, produced by Mut Lang, is considered by producers to this day as a reference standard for hard rock acoustics. "To this day, producers consider Back in Black a reference standard for hard rock acoustics."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Pour Some Sugar on Me Edition Part 1

podcast.title: Alice in Chains Vocal Harmonies
podcast.body: Alice in Chains was noted for having the best hard rock harmonies since the first version of Van Halen, specifically those between David Lee Roth and Michael Anthony. "Best hard rock harmony since, I don't know, David Lee Roth and Michael Anthony in the first version of Van Halen."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Groups That Changed Their Front-Person and Survived

podcast.title: Declining Appeal to Aging Baby Boomers (Late 1970s)
podcast.body: By the late 1970s, baby boomers in their late 20s and 30s, whose lifestyles had changed with "jobs and kids and cars and the car payments" and "house payments," found that "Hard rock on the whole was just maybe not as appealing" as it had been when they were younger. "Hard rock on the whole was just maybe not as appealing."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
srcs.episode: Ep. 51 - The Softer Side of 70s Rock

podcast.title: Evolving Definition of Rock Music
podcast.body: The definition of "rock music" as a whole is subject to change over time, making the precise categorization of subgenres like hard rock and heavy metal a fluid and sometimes debated matter. "It is important to keep in mind that the definition of rock music as a whole can and it does change."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
srcs.episode: Ep. 24 - Loud, Louder, Loudest - 70s Heavy Metal

podcast.title: Frowned Upon in Orange County
podcast.body: In Taylor Hawkins' early years in Orange County, California, hard rock was generally "frowned upon" by the local scene, which favored reggae. Those who listened to hard rock were often labeled "heshers" and were not considered "cool" or "surfers." "So hard rock was really frowned upon. You were a hesher. You were from the valley. You're not cool. You weren't a surfer."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Remembering Taylor Hawkins

podcast.title: Grammy Award for Linkin Park
podcast.body: Linkin Park's debut album, Hybrid Theory, was nominated for three Grammys, winning one in the category of Best Hard Rock Performance for their song "Crawling." "winning one for Crawling in the category of Best Hard Rock Performance."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Remembering Chester Bennington Part 1

podcast.title: Increased UK Chart Presence (2010s)
podcast.body: Hard rock, particularly groups from indie labels, saw an increased presence on the UK charts during the 2010s. "Heavy metal and hard rock, again, groups drawn largely from indie labels, saw an increased presence on the charts."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: Influence on Alt Hip Hop
podcast.body: The band Oxymorrons from Queens, New York City, are noted for their sound which incorporates a "Hard Rock Twist" into Alternative Hip Hop. "and you can call them Alternative Hip Hop with a Hard Rock Twist."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Black History Month 2023

podcast.title: Long Hair as a Standard
podcast.body: By the mid-1970s, long hair became a standard requirement in some quarters of music, particularly within hard rock and metal. This tradition continues today, cementing long hair as an expected aesthetic for these genres. "Long hair became standard in some quarters. Hard rock and metal often required it. That's a tradition that continues today."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rock Explainer 2

podcast.title: Origins in the Blues
podcast.body: Hard rock is characterized by its foundational roots, being "born out of the blues," a clear distinction from soft rock's origins in pop and folk music. "The soft rock is born out of pop and folk hard rock born out of the blues."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
srcs.episode: Ep. 51 - The Softer Side of 70s Rock

podcast.title: Precursor to Heavy Metal
podcast.body: Hard rock was the prevailing term used to describe the musical style that later became known as heavy metal during its formative years. Bands like Cream, categorized as hard rock, contributed elements that were foundational to the heavy metal genre before its distinct classification. "What we now know as heavy metal was usually referred to as hard rock."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
srcs.episode: Ep. 24 - Loud, Louder, Loudest - 70s Heavy Metal

podcast.title: Prominent Artists
podcast.body: Hard Rock is exemplified by bands like Jethro Tull and Rammstein, both of whom have had complex relationships with digital music platforms, particularly Spotify, often due to strong preferences for physical media or opposition to streaming's financial models. "la banda de Tull, la banda de Rock Duro... banda de rock, duro Ramstein"

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan
srcs.episode: Artistas que no están en Spotify y por qué

podcast.title: Sexual Undercurrent
podcast.body: Hard rock is notably associated with "a definite undercurrent" of sexuality. "The sexuality that is a definite undercurrent in hard rock."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
srcs.episode: Ep. 51 - The Softer Side of 70s Rock

podcast.title: Shift in UK Market Dominance
podcast.body: This increased chart presence marked a shift from a long period where American metal and hard rock bands, with few exceptions like Accept and Scorpions, largely dominated the British market. "And this was a nice change from a long stretch where American metal and hard rock bands pretty much had the British market to themselves, with a couple of bands like Accept and Scorpions thrown in."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 2: The Role of Indie Rock

podcast.title: The Runaways as Pioneers
podcast.body: The Runaways are considered the first all-female hard rock band in history to gain international attention. Their presence, led by Sandy West on drums, challenged gender norms in the male-dominated hard rock genre. "We can safely call them the first all-female hard rock band in history to receive international attention."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

podcast.title: Visual Comparison to Funk Albums
podcast.body: Earth Wind & Fire's albums, with their elaborate iconography, were noted to look more like progressive or hard rock albums, sitting comfortably in 70s LP collections next to acts like Led Zeppelin. "They looked more like progressive or hard rock albums, and they sat comfortably in the collections of 70's LP buyers, next to the likes of Led Zeppelin, and yes."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
srcs.episode: Give Up the Funk Edition Part 2
